text: DSH Study Mode 是一个面向 DSH 的学习教练模式，通过组合补丁注册主学习预设和内部练习员。它适合希望自己完成作业、学科题或编程练习的学生：默认先提问，再按 L0–L3 阶梯逐步给方向、关键线索或留空骨架；学科题一次只推进一步，概念问题可以直接讲解。模式还提供会话内练习清单和只读练习员，帮助生成变式题、核对思路。使用时需要 DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 或更新版本。

DSH Study Mode adds a study coach preset and practice agent. It guides homework and programming with L0–L3 hints, working through subject problems one step at a time while explaining concepts directly. A session list tracks exercises and sticking points. Requires DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 or newer.
想让 AI 陪我一步一步做作业，卡住时再给提示。
I want a study mode that guides me through a problem one step at a time instead of giving me the finished answer.
DSH Study Mode 的功能「逐级学习引导」：新题从 L0 提问开始，使用者请求提示后逐步升到 L1–L3；学科问题一次推进一个步骤，概念问题可直接解释。
DSH Study Mode 的功能「多题练习清单」：把一组题目整理成会话内清单，一次只推进一道，并记录微目标、状态和卡点；完成后可按卡点类型做练习小结。

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Why this exists：Hand your homework to an AI and it hands back something submittable in three seconds. You learn nothing in the process — the problem just moves from "I can't do this" to "I appear to be able to do this for now."

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Why this exists：This prompt takes the opposite approach: **ask, don't answer**. Hints are released one level at a time, and the highest level is a skeleton with the decision points left blank — not a finished answer. There is an explicit escape hatch if you genuinely want the complete answer, but you have to say so.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Why this exists：As a DSH mode there's an extra layer: **there is no shell, and no `write` / `edit` tools either**. Scaffolding a project, installing dependencies, running your code, writing a file — it can't do any of that. It isn't being asked nicely to hold back; the capability simply isn't there.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · What it is：Two agent presets, declared by a bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`): the main Study Mode, plus the internal `study-practice` agent it delegates to. Identity, toolset and sub-agent are composed when the session is created; the practice preset never shows up in the mode picker.

The default learner is a student working through **schoolwork**: maths, physics and chemistry problems go through the step-by-step protocol (decompose, one step per turn); programming keeps the original flow.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · What it is：| Layer | Contents | How it applies |
|---|---|---|
| Standing identity | Role, priority, bottom-line clause, level marker, fixed flow, the ladder, hard bans, pressure handling, the exit switch, a pre-send self-check | persona, **present on every request**, ~4,200 characters |
| On-demand detail | Seven skills: ladder detail, concept coaching, code debug coaching, review & progress, practice-agent protocol, subject step-by-step + sciences, writing | loaded by the model only when needed |
| Structural constraint | Toolset: **no shell and no `write` / `edit`**; the practice agent additionally has no `ask_user_question` and no delegation tools | fixed at session creation |

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Levels and the ladder：Every reply opens with its current level, like `[L1]`. Each new problem starts back at L0.

- **L0** (default): ask questions only, no substantive clue.
- **L1**: direction — which concept is involved, where to look.
- **L2**: key clue — the specific function/step/formula, or the API name, keyword or doc page to look up.
- **L3** (highest): a skeleton with blanks. The blanks must be the problem's real decision points, and the whole thing **must not run as-is**.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)：For schoolwork — maths, physics, chemistry, biology — the mode does **not** explain the whole solution. It decomposes the problem and advances **one step at a time**:
section: Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)：> Coach: what does the problem ask for? What do you think the first step is?
> Learner: find the acceleration… force analysis first?
> Coach: right, force analysis. Which forces, and which object?
> Learner: (states object and forces)
> Coach: the object is right. One force is missing — check what else touches this body.
> Coach: that step is done. What's the next step?
section: Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)

text: @dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)：Rules: he does a step, you judge that step, then ask for the next one; the L0–L3 ladder is used **inside** a step and only for the current step. The whole solution appears in exactly two places: the exit switch, or the demo channel (an analogous problem, same technique, neutral naming, followed by a faded practice — never the original problem).
section: Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)

text: @dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)：Each list entry carries a **micro-objective**, the **current step**, the level and the **stuck-point type**, so a compacted long session can pick up where it left off; the wrap-up reports the distribution of stuck-point types.
section: Subject problems: step by step (new in 2.1)

text:
@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · The practice contract：Hand it several problems at once and it opens a **practice list for the day** with `todo_write`: number, one-line topic, status. It asks which one you want to start with, then advances exactly one at a time. After each one it asks where you got stuck and what clicked, and compresses your answer into a few words appended to that entry. When everything is done it offers a short wrap-up (which ones went smoothly, which kind of step the sticking points clustered in).

Three deliberate choices:
@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · What's in it：One mode (plus an internal practice preset that never appears in the mode picker):

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · What's in it：- A standing rule set (~4,200 characters per request)
- Tools: `read` / `read_image` / `glob` / `grep` / `web_search` / `web_fetch` / `ask_user_question` / `skill` / `todo_write` plus sub-agent control (`send_message` / `interrupt_agent` / `list_agents`)
- **No** `pwsh` / `bash` / `jobs`, and **no** `write` / `edit`
- One read-only practice sub-agent (a separate preset, hidden from the mode picker by the roster shim)
- Subject step-by-step protocol: decomposition, one step at a time, stuck-point → hint-shape mapping, demo channel
- Web verification: formulas/theorems/APIs/textbooks/rubrics (links + quoted excerpts; never search for the original problem answer)
- Context compaction, so a long practice session doesn't grow until it overflows

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · What's in it：Seven skills ship inside the bundle and are discovered through `skill-filesystem`'s `customSkillDirs`, with the path resolved from the bundle's own location:

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · What's in it：| Skill | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `study-hint-ladder` | What each of L0–L3 may give, how to blank a skeleton, what counts as overstepping, when to raise or lower a level, stuck-point → hint-shape mapping |
| `study-concept-coaching` | Teaching a concept outright, verifying real understanding with 1–2 short checks, and not leaking the problem at hand |
| `study-debug-coaching` | The three opening questions for programming problems, guiding them to read their own error, reviewing without rewriting |
| `study-review-checklist` | When a review is actually warranted, how short it should be, the practice contract (list, state and stuck-point types), resetting between problems |
| `study-practice-subagent` | When to dispatch the practice agent, how to write the task, variant quality gates, timing, and enforcing "its output must never cover the original problem" |
| **`study-subject`** | **Step-by-step subject coaching: decomposition, one step per turn, a derivation-chain L3, the five common failure points, counter-example thinking** |
| `study-subject-writing` | Essays and text work: the hard rule that **not one complete sentence may be su

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · What's in it：The subject skills only swap out what a clue or a skeleton looks like; they do not override the bottom line or the process. Adding a subject means adding one directory under `skills/` — no preset change.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · The practice sub-agent：`subagent_practice`, read-only: `read` / `read_image` / `glob` / `grep` / `web_search` / `web_fetch`. No shell, no `write` / `edit`.

That read-only surface is a **structural guarantee**: the practice agent is its own agent preset (`study-practice`) whose plugin rows mount exactly those six tools. `write` / `edit` are never registered, and it has no `ask_user_question` and no delegation tools either.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · The practice sub-agent：Four jobs: **generate a variant** of the same concept, **independently check** the learner's answer (reporting which *kind* of step is wrong plus the criterion, never a fix), **supply counter-examples**, and **verify official documentation** (returning links and quoted passages).

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · The practice sub-agent：Its hard rule, written into both its persona and the dispatch skill: **never solve the learner's actual problem, never produce a submittable artifact.** If a task would violate that, it is supposed to refuse and offer an alternative.

Each `subagent_practice` call returns `started subagent <childId>` immediately (since 0.2.1 it always starts asynchronously — there is no `run_in_background` parameter); after that, dispatch with `send_message(agent_id: ...)` without restating the background.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · The practice sub-agent：The practice preset does not appear in the mode picker (the roster shim filters out **healthy** internal presets only). If it fails to load it shows up as a red card with the real error text, and the failure is also logged as `agent preset study-practice:` — so run the self-check and the real-host verification after structural edits.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Install：Repository: <https://github.com/Mashiro-Neri/dsh-study-mode>. Easiest is to install straight from GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Mashiro-Neri/dsh-study-mode
```

Needs DSH **0.2.1-rc.2 or newer** (`package.json` declares `engines.dsh`; older hosts cannot load the preset model). Three install paths, how to confirm it worked, and troubleshooting all live in **[INSTALL.zh.md](INSTALL.zh.md)** (Chinese). The shortest one:

```

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · In a fresh standard-mode session:：Afterwards, Settings → Modes should show a "学习模式" card, selectable on the new-session screen. That is the only new card — the internal practice preset is hidden by the roster shim. A session's mode is fixed at creation and cannot be changed later.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Distribution format：Built artifacts live in `dist/`: | File | Notes | |---|---| | `dsh-community-dsh-study-mode-2.2.1.tgz` | Installable npm package for `plugin_manager install_bundle`, or `dsh plugin --profile

add ` | | `…tgz.sha256` | SHA256 of the tarball | | `dsh-study-mode-2.2.1.zip` | **Whole-package archive**: source tree plus the tarball, self-contained — extracting yields a single top-level folder `dsh-study-mode-2.2.1/` | | `…zip.sha256` | SHA256 of the zip |

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Distribution format：**The two artifacts serve different purposes.** The `.tgz` is what DSH's `plugin_manager` consumes; the `.zip` is the human-facing bundle — unzip it and you have the source, the docs and working build scripts, no clone required. The tarball inside the zip matches its own bundled `.sha256`.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Distribution format：The zip holds 32 files (counting rule: one clean rebuild — `build-package.ps1` then `build-zip.ps1`: 30 files from the repository source tree plus the tarball and its sha256 in `dist/`; the zip being generated is not inside itself, and `.git` / `node_modules` are excluded):

```
dsh-study-mode-2.2.1/
├── src/                   source: persona Markdown + composition template
├── cordis.patch.yml       generated composition patch
├── package.json

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Distribution format：The package is `@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode`, declares `dsh.bundle.patch = ./cordis.patch.yml`, and its `files` allowlist ships only what's needed:

```
package/cordis.patch.yml         the preset declarations
package/plugin/hide-internal-presets.js  the roster shim
package/skills/…/SKILL.md        the seven skills
package/docs/source-prompt.zh.md the original prompt, for diffing against

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Distribution format：**Skill-path resolution handles both install layouts.** Linked locally the package is `@local/dsh-study-mode`; installed from a tarball, registry or git it is `@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode`. The patch's `!!js` expression walks a candidate list and takes the first one that resolves; when none resolves it **throws a readable error** instead of silently producing an empty skill directory. Hard-coding either name makes the other layout silently lose every skill — exactly the trap on your requirements-mode bundle.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Known tradeoffs and limitations：**`write` / `edit` are structurally absent now.** Both the main preset and the practice preset set `write: false` / `edit: false` on `tool-fs` — the tools are never registered, so this is no longer a rule the model is asked to follow. The cost is that the coach cannot write files for you either; it can only read.

**The shell is gone the same way.** No `pwsh` / `bash` / `jobs`: scaffolding, installing dependencies and running code are all impossible.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Known tradeoffs and limitations：**The practice agent's read-only surface comes from its own agent preset.** It mounts six tools, has no `ask_user_question`, and cannot delegate further. Its persona and toolset live in that preset; the delegation tool only points at it.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Known tradeoffs and limitations：**The practice preset is invisible in the mode picker, unless it breaks.** The roster shim filters healthy internal presets; a child preset that fails to load stays visible with its red "load failed" card and error text (and is also logged as `agent preset study-practice:`). Running `node scripts/check-bundle.cjs` and the real-host verification after structural edits catches most of it first.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Known tradeoffs and limitations：**The practice agent cannot see your conversation with the coach**, so every dispatch has to restate the background. The upside is that it never guesses at context it doesn't have.

**`send_message` has a timing constraint**: you cannot deliver while the practice agent is running — it returns `subagent "<id>" is unavailable`. Not a failure; wait for the round to finish.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Known tradeoffs and limitations：**The standing rules ride on every request**, around 4,200 characters (2.1.1 cut this back from 6,800 without changing any rule). The tradeoff is that the bottom line and the process skeleton must always be present, while detail loads on demand. Also note: the skill catalog is injected once per session (name + one-line description) and each skill body is loaded whole only when the `skill` tool is called; 2.1.1 shrank the catalog descriptions from 1,028 to 308 characters total.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Known tradeoffs and limitations：**The "Agent Teams" plugin no longer has to be off.** Since 0.2.1 a same-named tool registered in the preset scope shadows the global one: this mode's `send_message` takes `agent_id`, the teams version takes `target`, so the parameter name tells you which one you got.

@dsh-community/dsh-study-mode README · Hacking on it：The persona and the composition are **not hand-edited in `cordis.patch.yml`**: `src/persona.md`, `src/practice-persona.md` and `src/cordis.patch.template.yml` are the source, and the patch is generated. Edit Markdown for the persona, the template for the toolset, then re-render.

```powershell
